subject: Help with INLA SPDE Logistic regression model

messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Help with INLA SPDE Logistic regression model
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am running a spatial logistic regression model using the SPDE approach. My dataset is a point-level data which captures a mental health outcome (e.g. restorative benefit of a location coded as 0=No and 1=Yes). The data also contains sociodemographic and economic variables. 

I have been able to fit the model but having difficulty visualising the mean and SD of SPDE (e.g. model1$summary.random$spde$mean).My code for the model are below 

mesh3 <- inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain = loc, max.edge = c(1, 2.5),
                      offset = c(0.5, 0.5))
mesh3$n  #1380

#Create SPDE
cph.spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh3, alpha = 2,
                                prior.range = c(0.3, 0.5), # P(range < 0.3) = 0.5
                                prior.sigma = c(10, 0.01) # P(sigma > 1) = 0.01
)

indexs <- inla.spde.make.index("s", cph.spde$n.spde)
lengths(indexs)


A3 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh3, loc = loc)
dim(A3)   #1143 1380

#stack for estimate stk.e
stk.e <- inla.stack(
  tag = "est",
  data = list(y = SPDF$MNH, numtrials = 1),
  A = list(1, A3),
  effects = list(data.frame(sex=factor(SPDF@data$Sex)), s = indexs)
)

dim(inla.stack.A(stk.e))


formula <- y ~ 1 + sex + f(s, model = cph.spde)


res <- inla(formula,
            family = "binomial", Ntrials = 1,
            control.family = list(link = "logit"),
            data = inla.stack.data(stk.e),
            control.predictor = list(
              compute = TRUE, link = 1,
              A = inla.stack.A(stk.e)))

#summary of the intercept and covariate
res$summary.fixed

#summary of the precision of the Gaussian likelihood, i.e.,  
res$summary.hyperpar[1, ]


I tried this code for visualising the SPDE mean and sd


pgrid0 <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh3, xlim = 0:1, ylim = 0:1,
                              dims = c(2500, 2500))

prd0.m <- inla.mesh.project(pgrid0,  res$summary.random$s$mean)
prd0.s <- inla.mesh.project(pgrid0,  res$summary.random$s$sd)
 
but got NAs for the prd0.m and prd0.s matrices

Any help will be greatly appreciated. Thank you
